newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: India's import restrictions criticised at WTO.
newsitem.headline: India's import restrictions criticised at WTO.

text.p: India's trading partners expressed concern on Friday over quantitative import restrictions which still apply to some consumer goods, agriculture and textiles, trade sources said.
The European Union said India should graduate from a special dispensation under WTO rules, which allows it maintain restraint on imports for balance of payments reasons, they added.
The closed-door debate was held at the first meeting this year of the General Council of the World Trade Organisation.
It was the latest in a series of consultations since December 1995 aimed at phasing out Indian controls on products subject to balance of payment and quantitative restrictions.
India's delegation reiterated that it is willing to phase out the restirictions, but it must be gradual to maintain stability in line with reforms introduced since 1991.
"The general gist was much praise for India's economic reform efforts and for liberalisation in a variety of sectors," a trade source said.
"But some concerns remained about quantitative restrictions which apply on some 3,000 tariff lines including consumer goods, agriculture and textiles," he added.

The United States praised the Indian government's position on reform. It called for India to submit its report by the second week of May ahead of a June meeting at which a determination or final report on India's BOP position is due.
Japan supported the U.S. proposal, trade sources said.
India criticised comments by the EU and Switzerland which suggested that in some way India had not lived up to its multilateral trade obligations, they added.
"Ambassador (Srinivasan) Narayanan was clear on this point that there had been no failure to comply with obligations," a trade source said.
India's envoy said he would submit the report.
But he said the reform process in India would be given political support if the industrial countries would increase the market access opportunities for Indian goods, they added.
